items:
Return relay to service by removing the 
 test leads from the relay terminal block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads from the current terminals ( 5 - 6 ) , 
 voltage terminals ( 7 - 8 )
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact (1- 2 )

Make sure CT and PT secondary circuits 
 are in normal condition.

If any equipment associated with the 
 relay has been isolated, it should be returned to service by the following 
 restoration steps:
 - Breaker trip coils, - Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
 - Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.

text:
Protection
Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document lists the testing procedure P1, which must be performed on an 
annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above title block
These relays are designed for operation at rated system voltage to detect an 
 abnormal power flow in a given direction. for balanced load conditions only 
 one relay is required per terminal .
The 
 first draft initiated by eng. Fayza El-Sharkawy, tested by eng. Shirin 
 Hamdy & eng. Azza Salama at 23 April 2003, revised by EDEPCo., Quality Control 
eng. Adel El-Nagar, accepted by General Director eng. Mahmoud Saker, and approved 
 by eng. Moustfa Alam Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.
Safety Precautions
A work permit 
must be issued and the qualified test staff should carry the suitable 
safely category
A work permit 
must be issued and the qualified test staff should carry the suitable 
safely category
Safety fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area is required.
Tools and Equipment
Test Plug handle, Clamp ammeter.
Secondary injection test set OR 
 Double-F2200 test set
Test Leads.
Work to be Carried Out
Preparation
Make Sure C.T secondary circuit are opened at the incoming terminal blocks 
 before isolating the relay current circuit for test
Look 
 at field maintenance file and compare the position of the setting switches 
 on relay with those shown on the test sheet.
Testing the Relay 
Figure 1
Connect the test leads between current terminals ( 5 - 6 ).
Connect the test leads between the Voltage terminals ( 7 - 8 ).
Connect the test leads 
 between the trip terminals ( 1 - 2 )
Increase the voltage to 120 volt.
Increase the current slowly until the relay picks up.
Record the value of the current as the start current.
Increase the current to the value 5 x Istart then 10 x Istart.
Record the time, which the relay trips at every current value.
Return Relay and Associated Equipment to 
Service
Return relay to service by removing the 
 test leads from the relay terminal block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads from the current terminals ( 5 - 6 ) , 
 voltage terminals ( 7 - 8 )
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact (1- 2 )
Make sure CT and PT secondary circuits 
 are in normal condition.
If any equipment associated with the 
 relay has been isolated, it should be returned to service by the following 
 restoration steps:
 - Breaker trip coils, - Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
 - Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.
